subject: Cobalt Health discovery recap + proposed 30-day pilot
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoody.com>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@cobalthealth.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoody.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoody.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cobalt Health discovery recap + proposed 30-day pilot

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap and a concrete pilot proposal so we can move from conversation to work. 

Key pain points you called out:
- Production latency spikes when batching patient Q&A under peak hours (sustained 1800 reqs/min).
- Variability in hallucination rate on longer clinical-context prompts (~6% observed in your evals).
- High per-token costs when running ensemble reranking for accuracy-sensitive flows.
- Governance: need for audit logs and S3-level access controls for PHI handling.

Goals we aligned on:
- Reduce 95th pct latency to <= 250ms for single-turn clinical queries.
- Demonstrate quality lift (hallucination down to <2%) on a small, representative prompt set.
- Make per-interaction cost predictable (target ~40% reduction vs current orchestration).

Proposed 30-day pilot (summary):
- Scope: 30-day POC focused on the triage assistant workflow (incoming patient messages -> triage suggestion + confidence score).
- Throughput/scale: support up to 1,500 reqs/min with configured burst to 2,000 for testing.
- Evaluation: 400 prompt pairs (A/B) harvested from your anonymized logs; automated evals + small human review sample.
- Success metrics: 95th latency <= 250ms, hallucination rate <2% (measured by our eval harness), and 40% cost reduction on per-interaction basis after batching/quantization.
- Owners: Stephanie (sales, Redwood) / Ben (runtime lead) / Alyssa & Daniel (Cobalt product/tech).
- Access & safety: IP allowlist + temporary S3 bucket read-only access to sample anonymized logs; SOC2 evidence exchange via shared secure link.
- Timeline: Week 1 access & provisioning, Week 2 model selection + prompt tuning, Week 3 integrated evals, Week 4 ramp & measurement.

Immediate asks (what we need to start):
1) Alyssa — confirm the anonymized sample dataset: S3 bucket name and expected size (estimate>. 50MB).
2) Daniel — provide admin contact for network allowlist and any firewall constraints.
3) Cobalt — sign attached POC scope doc (POC_scope_v1.pdf) and confirm NDA/state of PHI handling.

I attached a one-page scope and a sample prompt set. If this looks good I’ll loop Ben and Marissa into a technical kickoff and propose times for Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood-inference.com | (415) 555-0196

Attachment: prompt_set_sample.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@cobalthealth.com>

Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cobalt Health discovery recap + proposed 30-day pilot

Thanks Stephanie — this is great and captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: we can provision a sanitized sample in S3 (bucket: cobalt-prod-sandbox, ~120MB gzipped). We’ll strip PHI but keep the conversational context. Is read-only IAM okay?
2) Firewall: we have a managed perimeter team — Daniel will send the allowlist contact and an internal ticket ID.
3) Eval cadence: can we include one weekly sync with a small panel of nurses for the human-review portion? That helps validate clinical relevance.

We also need to validate the quantization approach before ingesting samples — is Ben the right person to discuss numeric fidelity tradeoffs?

Confirming: we’re committed to the 30-day timeline and will sign the POC scope once legal does a quick check.

— Alyssa
Head of Product, Cobalt Health
alyssa@cobalthealth.com

Thanks, Alyssa — Ben here. Quick technical notes and what I’ll own on the POC: 

- Quantization/quality: I’ll run a small fidelity matrix on your sample prompts (FP16 vs 4-bit LLAMA-like quant) to compare EM/ROUGE-style metrics and hallucination proxies. I’ll share results in a short report within 3 business days of data access.
- Latency plan: we’ll prototype a trimmed attention kernel and prefix KV caching for the triage path to hit the 95th pctl SLA. Initial perf runs will use a 2-node dedicated pool (NVIDIA-grade GPUs) and a continuous-batching policy tuned to your workload.
- Observability: I’ll enable token-level traces (scrubbed for content) and per-request cost breakdown so we can measure the claimed 40% reduction.

Next steps I’ll take: create a sandbox deployment, send an allowlist IP range (will require your network contact), and pre-seed a prompt evaluation harness. Marissa — can you add the human-review workflow and weekly sync as a recurring item in the pilot calendar?

— Ben Carter
